statement: Supplementary Table S3 prints a mouse CSF volume of 0.04 mL and a non-human primate (NHP) CSF volume of 10 mL.
In that table a mouse dose of 8.00E+11 vg is 2.00E+13 vg/mL and its paired NHP equivalent is 2.00E+14 vg.
A footnote says the 2.00E+14 vg row was not included in the NHP toxicology study design.
The 3.05E+14 vg NHP dose is a maximum feasible dose set by NHP CSF volume, with no equivalent assessed in mice.

Table 4 gives a macaque CSF volume of 15 cm3. Its macaque row prints a surface-to-volume ratio of 6.8 although the same row's cells give (200+8)/90 = 2.3; the mouse, rat and human rows reproduce their printed ratios; the rat row reads 2.2 / 20 / 0.15 / 1 / 9.5.
In Study A, vehicle-group pre-dose antibody titres reach 10,240.
In Study B, vehicle-group pre-dose titres reach a printed log10 value of 5.44 (about 275,000).
A vehicle intrathecal animal reads 20,480 at day -15.
In Study 1 the buffer-control animal 38 has signal ratios 2.6 and 1.3 and is judged positive for both capsids, while the article text states that negativity for all AAVs was shown by Table S2.

statement: The cortical-neuron arm uses one dose (100 ng/mL) at one time (24 h); Figure 4B's two-way ANOVA prints F(1, 28); the legend does not state the unit of replication.
The paper's WWOX to JAK2/STAT3 interaction work uses cancer cells only, and its in vivo arms are overexpression experiments.

Under the lanes of panel L the printed values are 1 (JH WT), 0.2 (LM-iPS), and 0.4, 0.4, 0.9 (three AAV9 lanes); under panel M they are 1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 7 for JH WT, WPM S1, WPM D1, WPM D3, WPM S1 AAV9.
The original membrane for panel M holds seven sample lanes (JH WT, WPM S1, WPM D1, WPM D3, WPM S1 AAV9, WPM D1 AAV9, WPM D3 AAV9) whereas the published panel shows five.
The Methods say blots were repeated and quantified 2 to 3 times per experiment and that representative images of those repeats are shown.
The legend says panels L and M show the lines included in the single-cell RNA-seq experiment.
89 lymphoblastoid cell lines were analysed and the exon 8-9 versus exon 4-6 transcript comparison reports 88 lines.
The mean ratio of exon 8-9 to core (exons 4-6) transcription is 67 %, with intra-line correlation r = 0.68.
The alternative transcripts ending within intron 8 are attributed to GenBank database entries, not measured by the authors.
No splice-altering variant is assayed with the exon 8-9 junction amplicon in this paper.
The paper does not validate the junction assay for detecting loss of exon 9.
As designed, the assay cannot tell apart exon skipping, intron retention, use of a cryptic splice site and alternative termination.
